title: `pgrep -af godot` is case-sensitive, so it misses the official `Godot_v4.x...` editor binary, and it always lists the caller's own shell
evidence: The step tells the agent to run `pgrep -af godot` to decide whether the user has the project open, and to ask only when that doesn't settle it. `pgrep -f` matches the full command line case-sensitively; godotengine.org ships the binary as `Godot_v4.7-stable_linux.x86_64`, so an editor started from it isn't listed unless its path has a lowercase 'godot', and an empty result reads as 'no editor'. The calling shell's own command line contains 'godot', so the output is never empty either. The Claude
fix: Use `pgrep -afi godot`, say to ignore the shell's own line, and keep asking the user when the result doesn't settle it.
verified: Run against a process named `Godot_v4.7-stable_linux.x86_64`, `pgrep -af godot` did not list it while `pgrep -af Godot` did; with -f it also lists the calling shell's own `-c ... pgrep -af godot` line. The skill falls back to asking the user, so the effect is small.
